subject: GPA, coords.subset, meanshapes and data manipulation

messages.author: fcf9f47432524310
messages.subject: GPA, coords.subset, meanshapes and data manipulation
parts:
Hello  everybody,

currently I am doing some GM analysis head shape data with a 22 species with 148 specimens. But for three species I have only one specimen.
First I did the regular GPA and PCA stuff to see how the species occupy the morphospace.

Now I want to check for a effect of phylogeny using 'physignal' and plot a PCA with a phytree. Therefore, I want to use the mean shape of each species.
First question: Do I have to do the GPA for the entire dataset and then calculate the mean shape for each species or is it better to do GPA separately for each species, take the means of each species and do again a GPA with the mean shapes?
Second: I have tried to do the first option with 'coords.subset' as described in the example of the function

##assign group variable
groupspec<-factor(paste(classifier$genus,classifier$species))        #original length [1:148]                     
levels(groupspec)
####exclude levels with only n=1, as coords.subset does not work with them####
LMa<-ProcCoords_headlateral[,,148]
LMb<-ProcCoords_headlateral[,,142]
LMc<-ProcCoords_headlateral[,,143]

subsetLM<-ProcCoords_headlateral[,,c(1:141,144:147)]   #only specimens with n>1

sub_groupspec<-groupspec[c(1:141,144:147)]   #group variable with excluded specimens n=1

###do subset
new.coords_species<-coords.subset(A=subsetLM,group=sub_groupspec)
names(new.coords_species)
species.means<-lapply(new.coords_species,mshape)
###convert to array
species.means<-simplfy2array(species.means,higher=T)

Here I have the problem that the excluded species=specimens are still present as levels in the subset and in the array, but with empty values of course (see below). I just thought I could append the three specimens after that at the end of the array. But than I have still the empty fields.
How can I delete those "empty" landmark configuration from my array or fill those with the data I defined as LMa,b,c above, respectively? Or delete those levels from 'sub_groupspec'.

I hope my problem has become clear to you. Thank you already in advance!
Cheers,
Peter

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] GPA, coords.subset, meanshapes and data manipulation
parts:
Peter,

First, I believe that performing GPA on all individuals before finding means is the better option, but it is an idea that could be debated.  If you do GPA by species, obtain the means, then do GPA again on species means, you have decided that each species’ “weight” in the GPA should be the same whether it comprises 1 or many individuals.  If it were me, I would not want species represented by a single specimen to have excessive influence on the mean shape and alignment in GPA.

Second, I don’t understand why coords.subset does not work when there is only one specimen.  I tried to simulate this an example and it appears to work

> data("pupfish")
> group <- factor(c(rep(1,50), 2, 3,3,3)) # the 51st specimen is the only member of group 2
> gp.coods <- coords.subset(pupfish$coords, group = group)
> means<- lapply(gp.coods, mshape)
> sum(means[[2]] -  pupfish$coords[,,51])
[1] 0 # the mean of group 2 and specimen 51 are the same

Third, in the method you used, when you reduced your factor you did not re-factor.  This is a common problem when removing values, as the factor levels still exist.  For example:

> levels(group)
[1] "1" "2" "3"
> group2 <- group[-51]
> levels(group2)
[1] "1" "2" "3"
> group2 <- factor(group2)
> levels(group2)
[1] "1" “3"

You will notice that just by removing specimen 51, factor level “2” did not disappear unless I specifically redescribed the reduced variable as a new factor.  If you ask R to subset data or find means by factor levels and for one level, there are no data, it will return NaN values.  This is not a geomorph trait; it is an R trait.

Hope this helps!
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: GPA, coords.subset, meanshapes and data manipulation
parts:
I did state that earlier in the thread, trying to diagnose the error.  I just confirmed on my example though that if I give the specimens names and have only one specimen per group, I still get a result (and coords.subset does not attempt to change the names in any way).  In Alicia’s original query, I assumed that one specimen would be converted from an array to a matrix (R does that sometimes), which would throw off dimnames because there are only two dimensions for a matrix, while an array can haver 3 or more.  However, it appears not to be the case when I run it (an array with one specimen is returned). 

If you are having this issue, you might try:

dimnames(myCoords) <- NULL
newCoords <- coords.subset(myCoords, group)

You can after reassign specimen names after, if you like.

If that does not work, then there must be something wrong that is not apprent from the errors returned, and further investigation would be warranted.

Mike
